yieldos-dividend-tracker.overview:
Yieldos (styled YieldOS) is a web-based dividend tracker that frames your portfolio around the income it produces rather than its daily balance swings. Payouts are shown as upcoming paychecks on a calendar, and a FIRE projection estimates how many years remain until dividends could cover your expenses.

It supports US and Canadian (TSX) tickers, can import holdings from several large US brokers, and includes a strategy simulator you can try without an account. It suits income investors who mainly want to see when cash arrives and how close they are to financial independence.
features: Paycheck-style calendar of upcoming dividend payments
FIRE projection showing estimated years to freedom
Strategy simulator usable without signing up
Imports from Fidelity, Schwab, Vanguard and E*TRADE
Covers US and Canadian TSX tickers
Free ticker pages with pay schedules and yields
goodFor: Income investors tracking monthly cash flow
FIRE planners estimating a freedom date
consider: Built by a solo developer, so the feature set is still growing
Native mobile apps are not confirmed; it runs in the browser

top-dividend-etfs.overview:
Top Dividend ETFs is a free website that ranks roughly 100 dividend-focused ETFs and refreshes the data daily. Each fund shows its yield, assets under management, price history and a letter grade based on yield, issuer and price stability.

Visitors can filter by yield band, flag funds with price decay, and vote for a weekly favorite through a community poll. It works well as a quick starting point for comparing income ETFs side by side, especially for investors weighing high yield against share price erosion.
features: Daily-updated table of about 100 dividend ETFs
Filters by yield range and price decay
Letter grades based on yield, issuer and stability
Community voting for a weekly top ETF
goodFor: Spotting high-yield funds with price decay
consider: Focused on ETFs only, not individual dividend stocks
Rankings and votes are informational, not investment advice

weekly-etfs.overview:
Weekly ETFs is a free site dedicated to ETFs that pay distributions every week. It maintains a daily-updated list of more than 100 weekly payers with current yields, total returns and flags for funds whose share price has been eroding.

Alongside the database, it publishes ranked lists and articles and offers a calculator that estimates weekly income from a given investment. It is aimed at income investors curious about the fast-growing group of option-income and single-stock weekly funds, while reminding readers that many of these products carry high risk.
features: Live yields and total return figures
Price decay flags on eroding funds
Ranked lists and explainer blog posts
consider: Many listed funds are high-risk option-income products
Very high yields often come with share price erosion

growth-etfs-screener.overview:
Growth ETFs is a free, hand-picked directory of about 100 growth-oriented ETFs presented in a sortable, searchable table. Quick filters isolate large funds with over $1 billion in assets, funds with strong long-term returns, and the community's most-voted picks.

Users can build a watchlist, browse funds with a swipe-style tool and vote for favorites. It suits investors who want a simple way to scan growth ETFs before doing deeper research, and it pairs well with the dividend-focused sites in the same network.
features: Sortable, searchable table of about 100 growth ETFs
Quick filters for big AUM and high returns
Community voting with a Top 25 list
consider: Curated list, not a full-market ETF screener
Site is informational and does not give advice

devoted-dividends-youtube.overview:
Devoted Dividend Investing is a YouTube channel that teaches the fundamentals of dividend investing. Videos are faceless, narrated over screen recordings, and cover dividend stocks and ETFs, high-yield and dividend growth ideas, the dividend snowball approach and regular portfolio updates.

The channel connects to the creator's public portfolio dashboard at devoteddividend.com, so viewers can follow real holdings over time. It is a good fit for beginners and intermediate investors who prefer learning by watching and want a steady stream of practical, plain-language dividend content at no cost.
features: Dividend investing basics explained step by step
Covers dividend snowball and passive income strategy
goodFor: Viewers who like following a real portfolio
consider: Educational content, not personalized financial advice

seeking-alpha.overview:
Seeking Alpha is a large investment research platform combining crowdsourced analysis articles, news, earnings call transcripts and its own quantitative ratings. Dividend investors often use its Dividend Grades, which score safety, growth, yield and consistency, along with its stock screener.

A free account offers limited article access, while Premium unlocks full research, ratings, the screener and alerts, and lets you link brokerage portfolios. It suits self-directed investors who want deep coverage of individual stocks and are comfortable sorting through a wide range of author opinions.
features: Dividend Grades for safety, growth, yield and consistency
Stock screener with dividend and rating filters
Earnings call transcripts and real-time alerts
Mobile apps for phones and tablets
seeking-alpha.pricing: Free basic tier; Premium about $299/year, Pro about $2,400/year
goodFor: Deep research on individual dividend stocks
consider: Most ratings and articles sit behind the paid plan
Article quality varies because content is crowdsourced

google-sheets-dividend-tracker.overview:
The Google Sheets Dividend Tracker is a downloadable spreadsheet template sold on Gumroad by Dividend Empire, the creator behind the DevotedDividend brand. It is built to replace messy homemade spreadsheets with a ready-made layout for logging holdings and watching dividend income build up over time.

Because it is a one-time purchase that lives in your own Google account, there is no subscription and your data stays in a file you control. It suits hands-on investors who are comfortable in spreadsheets and prefer a simple, customizable tracker over a full portfolio app.
features: Tracks passive income growth over time
Data stays in your own Google account
goodFor: Investors who want to avoid subscriptions
consider: Holdings are entered manually rather than synced
Requires some comfort working in Google Sheets

drip-calculator.overview:
The DRIP Returns Calculator from Dividend Channel estimates how reinvesting dividends would have changed a stock's total return over a chosen period. It lets you compare the outcome of reinvesting payouts against taking them as cash.

The tool is free, though Dividend Channel asks visitors to register with a name and email after viewing several pages. The wider site also offers an ex-dividend calendar, a screener and dividend articles. It suits investors who want a quick historical look at the power of dividend reinvestment for a specific holding.
features: Estimates historical total return with dividends reinvested
Part of a site with ex-dividend calendar and screener
drip-calculator.pricing: Free; registration required after a few page views
goodFor: Seeing the long-term effect of DRIP
consider: Free registration with email is required for continued use
Looks backward at history rather than projecting future income

simply-safe-dividends.overview:
Simply Safe Dividends is a research and portfolio tracking service built for dividend investors. Its best-known feature is the Dividend Safety Score, which rates how likely a company is to cut its payout, alongside valuation charts, S&P credit ratings and dividend change alerts.

Subscribers can track unlimited portfolios, view an income calendar and forecast, screen stocks and closed-end funds, and follow model portfolios through a newsletter. It suits income-focused investors, including retirees, who want to judge payout reliability before buying and monitor it afterward.
features: Dividend Safety Scores to flag cut risk
Unlimited portfolios with income calendar and forecast
Valuation charts and S&P credit ratings
simply-safe-dividends.pricing: Paid; about $468/year (billed annually), free trial available
consider: No monthly billing option; annual plan only
Higher price than most basic dividend trackers

stock-unlock.overview:
Stock Unlock is an investment research and portfolio tracking platform covering over 170,000 stocks and ETFs on more than 70 exchanges. It scores each stock across categories including valuation, growth, profitability and dividends, and offers a screener with dozens of filters and an automated DCF calculator.

The portfolio tracker can sync with more than 30 brokerages, and apps are available for iOS and Android. A free plan covers the basics, while paid tiers add brokerage syncing and longer financial history. It suits newer and intermediate investors who want fundamentals and tracking in one affordable place.
features: Stock scores across seven categories including dividends
Screener with 85+ filters for stocks and ETFs
DCF calculator with up to 35 years of data
stock-unlock.pricing: Free plan; paid plans from about $7.50/month
consider: Ongoing brokerage sync and long history require a paid plan
Support is by email only

the-dividend-tracker.overview:
The Dividend Tracker is a portfolio app built specifically around dividend income. It pulls your holdings into one dashboard, projects upcoming payouts, shows a payment calendar, and sends alerts when ex-dividend dates approach or payouts change. It covers US, Canadian and UK tickers and supports many currencies.

The free tier is enough to try it with a small portfolio, while paid tiers remove ads, add automatic brokerage import, dividend grades and deeper metrics. It suits income investors who want a dedicated dividend tracker on the web or on their phone rather than a general market research site.
features: Dividend income projections and payout calendar
Alerts for ex-dividend dates and dividend changes
Automatic brokerage import on paid plans
Dividend grades and advanced metrics on Premium
API access and back-testing on Pro plan
goodFor: Investors with accounts at several brokers
consider: Free plan is limited to one portfolio and 10 holdings
Brokerage import requires a paid plan

marketbeat.overview:
MarketBeat is a financial data and news site that gathers analyst ratings, earnings, insider trades and dividend announcements into one place for individual investors. Dividend investors can use its dividend screener, dividend history pages and alerts for new declarations.

A free account offers a small watchlist and a daily newsletter. The All Access subscription adds unlimited watchlists, real-time email and text alerts, several screeners, research reports and portfolio syncing with major brokers through Plaid. It fits investors who like to follow analyst activity and corporate events closely.
features: Dividend screener and dividend announcement tracking
Analyst rating changes and price targets
Email and SMS alerts for dividends and ratings
Premium research reports and stock lists
marketbeat.pricing: Free plan; All Access $29/month or $249/year, 30-day free trial
consider: Most advanced tools require an All Access subscription
Site includes heavy promotional content and newsletter offers

stocktwits.overview:
StockTwits is a social network for investors and traders where posts are organized by ticker symbol. Users share short takes on stocks, ETFs and crypto, and the platform turns that chatter into sentiment readings and trending lists.

It is free to join, post, follow others and build watchlists. Paid plans remove ads and, with Edge, add sentiment history, expanded market data and advanced search. It suits investors who want a quick read on crowd sentiment around a ticker, though it is a discussion platform rather than a dedicated dividend tool.
features: Crowd sentiment indicators for stocks and crypto
Edge plan adds sentiment data and advanced search
consider: User posts are opinions and quality varies widely
Not built for dividend income tracking

blossom.overview:
Blossom is a social investing app where members can connect real brokerage accounts and share their portfolios, trades and ideas with a community of over 500,000 users. Linked accounts receive a verified badge, which adds credibility to what people post.

The free version includes the social feed, portfolio tracking and educational Learn and Earn content. The PRO tiers add dividend tracking and forecasting, sector and country exposure, benchmark comparisons and an AI assistant. It is a good fit for newer and dividend-focused investors, especially in North America, who enjoy learning alongside others.
features: Social feed of real, broker-linked portfolios
Portfolio tracking with brokerage account linking
Dividend tracking and forecasting on PRO
blossom.pricing: Free plan; PRO from $5.99/month billed annually ($8.99 monthly), 7-day trial
goodFor: Learning from other investors' real portfolios
consider: Dividend forecasting is part of the paid PRO tier
Community content is user generated and not advice

stockcharts.overview:
StockCharts is a long-running charting and technical analysis platform. It offers many chart styles, including candlestick, Point and Figure and Renko, along with dozens of indicators, saved ChartLists, scans that can run automatically, and price alerts. Its free ChartSchool library teaches charting concepts.

Basic charts and articles are free, and paid tiers unlock more indicators, alerts, saved layouts and advanced features. New members get a free first month. It suits investors who time entries with technical analysis, while dividend investors may find it most useful as a companion to a separate income tracker.
features: Candlestick, Point and Figure, Kagi and Renko charts
Dozens of technical indicators and overlays
Custom scans that can run daily
stockcharts.pricing: Free basic charts; paid plans from $19.95/month, first month free
consider: No dedicated mobile app, works through the mobile browser
Focused on technical analysis rather than dividend tracking

trading-view.overview:
TradingView is a charting platform and social network used by a very large community of traders and investors. It offers hundreds of built-in indicators, thousands of community scripts, many chart types and screeners for stocks, ETFs, bonds and crypto, plus fundamental data and portfolio tracking.

The free Basic plan covers simple charting with limits on indicators and alerts. Paid plans add more charts per layout, indicators, alerts and historical data. Users can also connect supported brokers to place trades from charts. It suits active investors and anyone who wants powerful charts across web, desktop and mobile.
features: Stock and ETF screeners with many filters
Trade from charts through supported brokers
Paper trading and community trade ideas
Synced layouts across web, desktop and mobile
goodFor: Investors who trade through a connected broker
consider: Free plan limits indicators, charts and alerts
Broker connections are aimed at trading, not dividend income tracking

investing.overview:
Investing.com is a large global financial portal offering quotes, news, charts and calendars for stocks, ETFs, currencies, commodities, bonds and crypto. Its free tools include an economic calendar, earnings and dividend calendars, price alerts and a portfolio tracker on the site and mobile apps.

The optional InvestingPro subscription adds fair value estimates, a deep stock screener, AI tools, billionaire portfolio tracking and an ad-free experience. It suits investors who want broad market coverage and calendars in one place, with the option to pay for more in-depth research.
features: Real-time quotes across many asset classes
InvestingPro fair value estimates and screener
investing.pricing: Free; optional InvestingPro subscription (Pro and Pro+), often discounted on annual plans
consider: Free version shows many ads
No free trial for InvestingPro was found

share-sight.overview:
Sharesight is an online portfolio tracker known for detailed dividend and tax reporting. It records dividends automatically across more than 700,000 stocks, ETFs and funds on 60+ exchanges, estimates future payouts, and includes a dividend calendar and future income report. Multi-currency portfolios and reinvested dividends are supported.

Holdings can be imported from hundreds of brokers, through trade confirmation emails or spreadsheet uploads. A free plan covers up to 10 holdings, with paid tiers adding more holdings and portfolios. It suits dividend investors who hold international shares or need clean records for tax time.
features: Future income report and dividend calendar
share-sight.pricing: Free plan (10 holdings); paid plans from $7/month billed annually
consider: Free plan is limited to one portfolio and 10 holdings
Automatic DRIP handling is limited to some exchanges

stock-analysis.overview:
StockAnalysis.com is a fast, clean research site with financial statements, statistics, ETF holdings, dividend history and screeners for over 130,000 global stocks and funds. Much of the data is free to browse.

The Pro subscription unlocks longer financial and dividend history, more watchlist and alert capacity, full ETF holdings, analyst tracking and data downloads to Excel, CSV or Google Sheets. Portfolios can be synced from brokerage accounts. It suits investors who want straightforward fundamental data, including decades of dividend history, without a cluttered interface.
features: Up to 50 years of dividend history on paid tiers
Data downloads to Excel, CSV and Google Sheets
stock-analysis.pricing: Free plan; Pro $9.99/month or $79/year, 60-day money-back guarantee
consider: Pro tier limits data downloads to one per day
Deepest history and unlimited features need the higher tier

fast-graphs.overview:
FAST Graphs, short for Fundamental Analysis Software Tool, is a research platform built around valuation charts. Its signature graphs plot a company's share price against its earnings or cash flow history, making it easier to see whether a stock looks cheap, fair or expensive relative to its fundamentals.

It also includes dividend history, portfolio tools with dividend income projections, an FG Score for quality, and an AI assistant for screens and analysis. Premium supports broker connections. It suits long-term value and dividend growth investors who want to judge valuation before buying.
features: Multiple valuation metrics including cash flow and EBITDA
AI assistant for screens and analysis
fast-graphs.pricing: Paid; from $15.95/month billed annually, 7-day free trial
goodFor: Checking if a stock is over or undervalued
consider: No free plan beyond the trial
Basic plan excludes several metrics and screen building

snowball-analytics.overview:
Snowball Analytics is a portfolio and dividend tracker that pulls holdings from many accounts into a single dashboard. It can connect to more than 1,000 brokerages through aggregators like Plaid, Yodlee and SnapTrade, or accept CSV, Excel and PDF statement imports.

For income investors, it shows upcoming payouts on a calendar, projects future dividend income, rates dividend safety and models DRIP compounding. It also offers ETF look-through, allocation analysis and true return figures (TWR and IRR). It suits dividend investors who hold positions at several brokers and want automated tracking.
features: Auto-sync with 1,000+ brokerages, plus file imports
Dividend calendar and future income projections
Dividend safety rating and dividend stock screener
ETF look-through to see underlying holdings
snowball-analytics.pricing: Free plan (1 portfolio, 10 holdings); paid plans from $79.99/year with 14-day free trial
goodFor: Dividend investors with multiple brokerage accounts
consider: Free plan is capped at 10 holdings and lacks brokerage linking
Most advanced features require an annual paid plan

cnbc.overview:
CNBC is a major business news network, and its website and app carry market news, live quotes, interactive charts and video from the TV channel. Users can build watchlists and receive breaking news alerts by topic.

It is a news and market-data source rather than a dedicated dividend tool, so it works best for keeping up with earnings, economic data and company headlines that can affect income holdings. A paid CNBC Pro tier adds analyst insights, a stock screener and full show episodes, and a separate Investing Club subscription is also offered.
features: Real-time business and market news coverage
Customizable watchlists, up to 100 in the app
Live TV previews, podcasts and video clips
goodFor: Following daily market and company news
Investors who want quick quotes and headlines
consider: Not built for dividend tracking or income planning
Some in-depth content sits behind the CNBC Pro paywall

etf-comparison.overview:
ETF Comparison is a free tool on etf.com that places two ETFs side by side so investors can see how they differ. It groups the comparison into sections covering fund facts, costs, performance, portfolio makeup, factor exposure and ESG metrics.

The cost section looks at expense ratios, trading spreads and tracking differences, while the portfolio section shows sector weights and top 10 holdings. It is useful for anyone choosing between two similar funds, such as two dividend ETFs, and wanting a quick read on fees, returns and holdings before buying.
features: Expense ratio, spread and tracking difference data
Overlay performance charts and trailing returns
goodFor: Comparing fund costs and performance quickly
consider: Compares only two funds at a time
Does not track your own portfolio or dividend income

etf-research-center.overview:
ETF Research Center (ETFRC) is a fund research site whose best-known feature is its Fund Overlap tool. You enter two equity ETFs and it reports how much of their weight is in shared holdings, how many holdings they have in common and which top positions overlap.

It also shows sector drift and the stocks one fund overweights relative to the other. The wider site includes an ETF finder, a screener, a stock locator that shows which ETFs own a given stock, and a cost of ownership comparison. It suits investors checking whether two funds really add diversification.
features: Overlap percentage by weight between two ETFs
Count and list of shared holdings
Stock locator showing which ETFs hold a stock
ETF screener and total cost of ownership comparison
etf-research-center.pricing: Free; free registration unlocks full overlap lists; premium tier available
goodFor: Avoiding redundant funds in a portfolio
consider: Overlap tool compares two funds at a time
Full list of shared holdings requires a free account

market-chameleon.overview:
Market Chameleon is a research platform aimed mostly at options and event-driven traders, with tools for implied volatility, unusual options activity, earnings moves and multi-leg strategy screening. It also includes a dividend section with a dividend calendar, upcoming ex-dividend dates and lists of recent dividend increases.

Many pages are free to view, and a premium subscription unlocks deeper historical data, advanced screeners and data downloads, including dividend data. It suits active traders who want dividend dates alongside options and earnings data, more than buy-and-hold investors.
features: Dividend calendar with upcoming ex-dividend dates
Options volatility and unusual activity tools
Earnings calendar and implied move analysis
market-chameleon.pricing: Free tools; Premium is $99/month with a 7-day free trial
goodFor: Options traders planning around ex-dividend dates
Active traders who want event and earnings data
consider: Interface and tools lean toward options trading
Premium plan is pricey for casual dividend investors

yahoo-finance.overview:
Yahoo Finance is a widely used financial portal with free quotes, charts, news, company financials and dividend history for stocks and ETFs. Users can create watchlists and portfolios, and in the US they can link brokerage accounts through Yodlee so balances and holdings update automatically.

Paid tiers (Bronze, Silver and Gold) add portfolio risk and diversification analysis, Morningstar ratings, fair value and dividend scores, research reports and historical data downloads. It suits nearly every investor as a free starting point for looking up yields, payout history and news.
features: Free quotes, charts and dividend history
Company financial statements and key statistics
Paid tiers add research reports and dividend scores
yahoo-finance.pricing: Free; paid plans from $7.95/month billed yearly, up to $39.95/month for Gold
goodFor: Quick lookups of yields and payout history
consider: Brokerage linking is available in the US only
Free version shows ads and some data is paywalled

morningstar.overview:
Morningstar is an investment research firm known for its star ratings on funds and its analyst research on stocks. The paid Morningstar Investor service adds Medalist ratings for funds, fair value estimates for stocks, screeners and the Portfolio X-Ray tool.

X-Ray breaks down a portfolio by asset allocation, sector, fees and overlapping holdings. Accounts can be linked through Morningstar ByAllAccounts so holdings update automatically. It suits investors who rely on ETFs and mutual funds and want independent ratings and fee analysis before buying.
features: Star and Medalist ratings for funds and ETFs
Portfolio X-Ray for allocation, fees and overlap
morningstar.pricing: Some free content; Morningstar Investor is $34.95/month or $249/year, with a free trial
goodFor: Investors who value independent analyst ratings
Checking fees and overlap across holdings
consider: Most ratings and research require a paid subscription
Less focused on dividend income tracking than dedicated trackers

tipranks.overview:
TipRanks is a stock research platform built around tracking the recommendations of Wall Street analysts, corporate insiders, hedge funds and financial bloggers, and ranking how well each has performed. Its Smart Score rolls several data sets into a single rating for each stock.

The free version includes screeners, charts and watchlists, while Smart Scores, price targets and top-pick lists sit behind paid plans. Investors can also connect a brokerage portfolio for tracking and alerts. It suits investors who want to see what analysts and other experts think before buying a dividend stock.
features: Smart Score rating for each stock
Insider and hedge fund activity tracking
tipranks.pricing: Free plan; paid plans billed annually, with Premium around $360/year
goodFor: Seeing analyst and expert sentiment on stocks
Investors who want a single summary score
consider: Paid plans are annual only, with no monthly option
Key data like Smart Scores is locked on the free plan

portseido.overview:
Portseido is a portfolio tracker that follows investments across more than 70 stock exchanges, thousands of ETFs and cryptocurrencies, and can show results in any currency. It records dividends and stock splits automatically and keeps dividend history alongside projections of future payments.

Performance can be measured with simple return, time-weighted return or money-weighted return, and portfolios can be benchmarked against an index. Multiple portfolios can be combined into one view on paid plans. It suits globally diversified investors who want clear performance math and dividend tracking without a cluttered interface.
features: Coverage of 70+ exchanges, ETFs and crypto
Automatic dividend and stock split tracking
Dividend history and future income planning
Simple, TWR and MWR return calculations
portseido.pricing: Free plan (up to 50 transactions); paid plans from about $8/month
goodFor: Investors holding assets on multiple global exchanges
consider: Free plan is limited to 50 transactions and one portfolio
Android app availability not confirmed

schd-calculator.overview:
The SCHD Calculator from TopDividendETFs.com is a free web tool that estimates the income from the Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD). You enter how many shares you own or plan to own, and it shows current annual and quarterly dividend income based on the trailing twelve-month payout.

You then pick an annual dividend growth rate between 7% and 11% and a time frame of 5 to 30 years to see a year-by-year projection with charts. It suits SCHD holders who want a quick, sign-up free look at how their income could grow.
features: Current annual and quarterly SCHD income estimate
consider: Covers SCHD only
Does not model contributions, DRIP or taxes

top-monthly-dividend-etfs.overview:
Top Monthly Dividend ETFs is a free website (MonthlyETFs.com) that lists ETFs and funds paying distributions every month. Each entry shows the ticker, fund name, dividend yield, assets under management and a simple price decay flag that notes whether the share price has fallen since the fund launched.

The table can be filtered by yield band and by price decay, and linked fund pages add income calculators. It suits income investors who want a fast way to compare monthly payers, especially covered call and option income funds. The site labels itself educational only, so figures should be checked before acting.
features: Curated table of monthly paying ETFs and funds
Shows yield, AUM and price decay status
Filter by yield range and price decay
Per-fund data pages with income calculators
goodFor: Screening out funds with price erosion
consider: Price decay is a simple yes/no based on share price since inception
Not a portfolio tracker; no account or holdings import

drip-performance-simulator.overview:
DRIP Performance Simulator is a free backtesting tool on the Wolf of Options website that compares how high-yield funds would have performed with different levels of dividend reinvestment. You enter up to eight tickers, a starting amount or share count, and a date range, then set what percentage of each payout gets reinvested.

Results show ending shares, total dividends, amounts reinvested versus withdrawn, principal return, total return and CAGR, plus a chart. It is a good fit for investors weighing whether to live off distributions or reinvest them, particularly with covered call and option income ETFs.
features: Compare up to eight tickers side by side
Reports principal return, total return and CAGR
Chart of results after each run
goodFor: Comparing high-yield ETFs on total return
consider: Backtests show past results only, not future returns
Simple single-page tool without saved portfolios

hey-dividend.overview:
Hey Dividend (HeyDividend) is a dividend-focused portfolio platform that pairs holdings tracking with an AI chat assistant and machine learning dividend scores. It covers stocks, ETFs, CEFs, BDCs and REITs, and adds tools such as forward income projections, NAV erosion analysis and a dividend calendar.

The free plan covers one portfolio of up to 25 holdings, while Pro adds unlimited portfolios, real-time data, a prediction engine and broker sync through Plaid. Every new account gets a 14-day Pro trial. It suits income investors who want alerts on dividend safety and capital erosion alongside basic tracking.
features: AI chat assistant for dividend questions
NAV erosion analysis for income ETFs
Forward income projections and goal tracking
Broker sync via Plaid on Pro
hey-dividend.pricing: Free plan; Pro $9.99/month or $79.99/year, 14-day Pro trial
consider: Broker sync and real-time data require Pro
Free plan limited to one portfolio of 25 holdings

harvey-ai.overview:
Harvey AI (theharvey.ai) is an AI assistant aimed at investors, listed in our directory for research, news, dividend calculations and tracking.

We could not load its website during our most recent check, so features and plans are not shown here yet. Visit the site for its current offering before signing up.
consider: Separate company from Harvey, the legal AI firm

yieldcanary.overview:
YieldCanary is a research and tracking platform built around the health of income ETFs, mainly covered call and option income funds, with more than 320 funds covered. Each fund gets a status rating, a yield figure that strips out return of capital, an estimated runway before heavy NAV erosion, and full distribution history.

The portfolio side estimates after-tax monthly income, lays out a payout calendar and sends a monthly summary email. It suits investors holding high-yield option income ETFs who want to spot yield traps. A free tier exists, and paid plans include a 7-day trial that requires a card.
features: Yield figure with return of capital removed
Distribution calendar and monthly email summary
Curated lists like best monthly payers
yieldcanary.pricing: Free plan; Basic $9/month, Advanced $19/month; 7-day free trial
goodFor: Covered call and option income ETF holders
Spotting yield traps and NAV decay
consider: Brokerage syncing is listed as coming soon
Coverage currently centered on option income ETFs

dividend-decoder.overview:
Dividend Decoder is the fund research tool on CashStreams.io that looks past headline yield to judge whether a payout looks sustainable. It tracks 529 dividend-focused funds across ETFs, REITs, BDCs, CEFs and other income strategies, with data refreshed monthly.

Each fund report reviews payout support, price trend, total return, dividend history, drawdown and volatility. The site also shows a monthly payout timeline with confirmed and estimated distributions, plus lists of funds whose yields or growth changed most. It suits income investors trying to avoid yield traps before buying a high-yield fund.
features: Price trend, total return and drawdown data
Monthly payout timeline with confirmed and estimated amounts
Lists of biggest yield and growth changes
dividend-decoder.pricing: Free (no paid plans shown on site)
goodFor: Checking if a high yield is sustainable
Researching REITs, BDCs, CEFs and ETFs
consider: Signals update monthly, not in real time
Research tool only; no portfolio tracking

foliofox.overview:
Foliofox is a free, open-source portfolio tracker that brings holdings from many accounts and asset types into one dashboard. It covers stocks, ETFs, crypto, cash, real estate and private investments, and keeps a running history of net worth.

An AI advisor uses your actual portfolio data to offer insights, and scenario planning tools help with long-term goals. Holdings can be entered manually or imported from brokers. It suits investors spread across several brokers, currencies or alternative assets who want a single view of their wealth. The product is labeled beta and its homepage is quite minimal.
features: Tracks stocks, ETFs, crypto, cash and property
Net worth history and asset allocation views
AI advisor based on your own holdings
goodFor: Investors with many accounts and asset types
consider: Still in beta
Not built specifically for dividend tracking

surmount-ai.overview:
Surmount is an automated investing platform that lets self-directed investors run rules-based strategies in their own brokerage accounts. You can pick from a marketplace of prebuilt data-driven portfolios or build your own with no-code, code or AI strategy builders.

Surmount connects to many outside brokerage accounts and handles trade execution, rebalancing and tracking. Paper trading is available for testing ideas. It suits investors who want automation and systematic strategies rather than a pure dividend tracker. A free tier exists, with paid tiers adding more builders and connected accounts.
features: No-code, code and AI strategy builders
Connects to many external brokerage accounts
surmount-ai.pricing: Free plan; paid plans from about $5/month
consider: Places trades automatically, so review strategy risk
More of an automation tool than a dividend tracker

etf-total-returns.overview:
ETF Total Returns (ETFTotalReturns.com) is a free website that ranks ETFs by total return and annualized return alongside their dividend yield and inception date. The goal is to show whether a high yield has actually translated into growth once price changes are counted.

The table can be searched and filtered by yield range and by positive or negative returns. Clicking a fund opens a scorecard with a grade, an income calculator and head-to-head comparisons. It suits income investors comparing high-yield ETFs. Extra data such as tax treatment and price decay sits in a separate paid PRO product.
features: Total and annualized returns next to yield
Filter by yield range and return direction
goodFor: Checking yield against real total return
consider: Site notes data may be inaccurate and is for entertainment only
Advanced filters and extra data require PRO

portfolioglance.overview:
PortfolioGlance is a free portfolio tracker that rebuilds your history and performance from what you hold today, so you do not need to log every trade. Holdings can be typed in, imported from a CSV or broker statement, or read from a screenshot of your positions.

It supports unlimited portfolios, more than 30 currencies, benchmark comparison and allocation drift alerts. AI features include news-based analysis of individual holdings and a portfolio roast written in the style of famous investors. It suits investors who want a simple net worth view without linking brokerage logins.
features: Import from CSV, statements or screenshots
Benchmark comparison and allocation drift tracking
AI analysis of holdings using recent news
Portfolio roast in legendary investor styles
portfolioglance.pricing: Free; pay only for extra AI analysis beyond the included allowance
consider: No automatic broker linking; updates are manual or by import
Not focused specifically on dividend income

merrydiv-dividend-tracker.overview:
MerryDiv is a dividend income tracker built for investors whose main goal is passive income. It links to brokerage accounts through Plaid with read-only access, pulls in holdings and dividend payments, and rolls everything into one dashboard showing monthly income and a forward 12-month projection.

Beyond tracking, it includes a dividend calendar, diversification breakdowns by sector, country and asset type, and research lists such as Dividend Aristocrats and Kings. It suits people holding dividend stocks and ETFs across several accounts, such as a Roth IRA, 401(k) and taxable account, who want a single income view.
features: Sector, country and asset-type diversification views
Dividend Aristocrats and Kings research lists
goodFor: Tracking several accounts in one place
consider: Free plan syncs only one brokerage
No Android app was confirmed

stockoscope.overview:
StockoScope is a web-based stock research platform covering more than 3,000 US-listed companies. Rather than giving each stock one blended rating, it scores companies on five separate dimensions (Quality, Peers, Valuation, Analysts and Holdings) and shows them side by side, with the math behind each score visible.

Users can adjust weights, build Quality, Value or Dividend strategies, and filter the market with a screener that includes preset strategies. It suits long-term, research-minded investors who want transparent scoring they can customize instead of buy or sell calls.
features: Valuation via DCF and dividend discount models
stockoscope.pricing: Free plan; Pro $15/month or $150/year, 14-day Pro trial
consider: Covers US-listed stocks only
Free plan limited to 3 deep-dives per month

equity-rank.overview:
Equity Rank is a web-based stock valuation and screening service covering more than 3,000 US stocks. It estimates fair value using 19 valuation models, including several DCF variants and the Graham Number, and combines them with sentiment, analyst and earnings-quality data into a composite score it calls SAVE, refreshed daily.

Its higher tier adds AI-written analyses and an options screener with implied volatility data and wheel strategy candidates. It suits self-directed investors who want quick fair value estimates and a systematic ranking to narrow down ideas.
features: 19 fair value and intrinsic value models
Screener by score, sector and valuation
Portfolio scoring via brokerage CSV upload
consider: Portfolio import is manual CSV upload, not live sync
Options and AI tools require the pricier Pro plan

trade-time.overview:
Trade Time is a free, simple reference site that shows the regular trading hours of 30 major stock exchanges around the world, converted into your own local time zone. Exchanges are grouped by region, covering the Americas, Europe, Africa, Asia and Oceania.

It is handy for investors who hold international stocks or ETFs and want to know when markets such as London, Tokyo, Hong Kong or Toronto are open without doing time zone math. It also shows exchanges with a midday lunch break, such as Tokyo, Shanghai and Hong Kong.
features: Trading hours for 30 major global exchanges
Hours converted to your local time zone
Grouped by region: Americas, Europe, Asia and more
Shows midday breaks on Asian exchanges
Covers NYSE, NASDAQ, London, Tokyo and more
goodFor: Checking when foreign markets are open
consider: Reference tool only, with no quotes or portfolio tracking

alphaos.overview:
AlphaOS is an investment research platform that organizes information around themes and company relationships rather than single ticker news. Users follow themes such as AI infrastructure or semiconductors, watch individual stocks, and get flagged when something material changes, along with an explanation of how it may affect suppliers, customers and competitors.

It draws on filings and earnings calls, uses a knowledge graph of company and industry links, and offers ETF look-through and side-by-side comparisons. It suits active investors and analysts who think in themes and supply chains, more than income-focused dividend investors.
features: Alerts on material developments with context
consider: Not focused on dividend or income tracking
Pricing could not be confirmed during review

gravel-calculator.overview:
Gravel Calculator (calcgravel.com) is a free online calculator for construction and landscaping projects. Based on the site's own description, it estimates how much gravel a project needs in tons and cubic yards and gives an approximate material cost.

It can help homeowners and contractors plan driveways, paths and similar jobs. It is not a financial or investing tool, and it does not calculate dividends, returns or portfolio values, despite being submitted under that category.
features: Free to use in a browser
consider: Not an investing or dividend tool at all
Site details beyond its basic purpose could not be fully loaded

tradecompass.overview:
TradeCompass is a web app that produces AI-generated analysis reports for stocks, ETFs, forex and crypto. You enter a ticker and get a structured report with trend signals, support and resistance levels, indicators like RSI, MACD and ADX, related news, and a buy, hold or sell style signal with a confidence score.

It was built with Canadian investors in mind, adding context for TFSA and RRSP accounts and TSX coverage. It suits shorter-term traders and investors who want a fast technical snapshot rather than deep fundamental or dividend research.
tradecompass.pricing: 2 free reports; paid via per-report credits or monthly plan
consider: Mostly technical and signal based, not dividend focused
Exact paid prices were not listed on the site

prismiva-portfolio-x-ray.overview:
Prismiva Portfolio X-Ray is a free check that shows how concentrated your portfolio really is. You type in your tickers and approximate market values (or import a CSV), and it measures your largest single position, how much rides on your top three holdings, sector exposure, and how many holdings you effectively own once weights are considered.

The check runs in your browser with no account and no holdings uploaded. It suits investors with several accounts who want a quick reality check on diversification. A free Prismiva account adds a broader portfolio workspace with optional read-only brokerage linking.
consider: Educational check only, it does not weigh goals or taxes
Brokerage linking is optional and only in the full workspace

crowdwisdom-trading.overview:
CrowdWisdom Trading is a market research service that uses AI to scan publicly shared views from thousands of traders on YouTube, Reddit, X and trading communities, then turns the strongest consensus into trade ideas with entry, stop and target levels. It covers US stocks, forex, crypto and commodities, and publishes a public track record of its calls.

Ideas arrive through a web dashboard, email briefings and Telegram channels. It suits active traders who want sentiment-driven setups, and it states clearly that it offers education and research, not investment advice.
features: Trade ideas with entry, stop and targets
consider: Trading-focused, not built for dividend investors
Track record figures are self-reported
